stories.delivered_paragraph: The White House will meet AI companies Tuesday to review a voluntary framework for testing the cybersecurity capabilities of the industry’s most advanced models. The framework was ordered by President Donald Trump in June, and Anthropic, OpenAI and Google are expected to participate, according to sources cited by CNBC and The Information. The effort signals that the administration is seeking common safeguards for increasingly capable models without imposing a mandatory regime.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Toni Schneider has formally taken over as Bluesky’s CEO after serving briefly on an interim basis, while former chief Jay Graber becomes chief innovation officer. Schneider inherits both Bluesky’s consumer social app and its underlying AT Protocol, which lets outside developers build interoperable social products in an expanding ecosystem known as the ATmosphere. His challenge is to broaden the service beyond a like-minded user bubble while preserving user control and the protocol’s open ambitions.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Russian anti-war politician Boris Nadezhdin says he has left Russia after authorities labeled him a “foreign agent” last month, posting a video from Paris saying he was alive and free. His departure further narrows the space for anti-war political opposition inside Russia.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Attacks on vessels in the Red Sea have made the threat to Middle East oil shipping its worst since the Iran war began, analysts say, as tankers also avoid the blocked Strait of Hormuz. Only eight ships used the strait Sunday, versus more than 100 daily before the war, and roughly 20% of global oil and gas had previously moved through it. Disruption across both routes is tightening a crucial energy chokepoint and raising risks for global supplies.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Myanmar’s military government released photos showing detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi meeting an International Committee of the Red Cross official, the first confirmed outside contact in 2.5 years. stories.delivered_paragraph: The Radio Hall of Fame named nine posthumous Legends inductees for 2026, including broadcaster and game-show host Wink Martindale, Vee-Jay Records co-founder Vivian Carter and radio executive Gary Krantz. Other honorees are D.E. “Duke” Wright and on-air personalities Lin Brehmer, Dale Dorman, B. Mitchell Reed, Pierre Robert and Polito Vega. The selections recognize figures whose work ranged from local radio to record-label and syndication businesses that shaped the medium’s reach.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Garena will bring “Palworld” to iOS and Android later this year with “Palworld Online,” an open-world MMORPG based on the PC survival and creature-collecting game. stories.delivered_paragraph: Amazon’s market value topped $3 trillion for the first time after its shares rose roughly 4% to a record high Monday, extending a post-earnings rally. Second-quarter revenue reached $200.61 billion, above the $196.47 billion analysts expected, while AWS revenue climbed to $42.2 billion on AI demand. Amazon also raised its 2026 capital-expenditure estimate to $220 billion, showing that its cloud growth is coming with an increasingly costly race to add computing capacity.
